sampled-sequences.warm_up: The eight integer samples [0, 8192, 0, -8192, 0, 8192, 0, -8192] were recorded at 8 kHz by a signed 16-bit ADC with ±2 V full scale. Label every sample by n and nT_s, convert the codes to volts, and report the sample span and repeating-cycle frequency with units. Check that the last timestamp is 7T_s rather than 8T_s.
sampled-sequences.strategy_choice: For (a) comparing two stored buffers sample by sample and (b) estimating the physical waveform halfway between samples, choose respectively between sequence-domain analysis and continuous reconstruction under an explicit interpolant. The deciding cue is whether the claim concerns recorded sample values or unobserved between-sample behavior. Produce a two-row decision table naming the representation, required metadata, and one claim each method cannot support.

impulse-response-and-convolution.warm_up: For x=[1,2] starting at n=0 and h=[1,-1] starting at n=0, compute every sample and support index of the linear convolution. Verify [1,1,-2] twice: once by the convolution sum and once by adding one copy of h to a two-times shifted copy. State the zero-padding convention used at the boundaries.
impulse-response-and-convolution.strategy_choice: Choose between flip-and-slide convolution and a Toeplitz-matrix product for (a) explaining which tap creates each output sample of x=[1,2] with h=[1,-1] and (b) applying the same three-tap kernel to 100 short records in one array operation. The cue is whether contribution-level interpretation or repeated structured computation is the priority. Produce the selected setup for each case and verify both yield [1,1,-2] on the canonical record.

difference-equations-and-stability.warm_up: Starting from rest, drive y[n]=0.5y[n-1]+x[n] with x[n]=delta[n]. Compute y[0] through y[5], identify the homogeneous mode, and sum the infinite absolute impulse response. Check the result against the BIBO condition and report the settling index at which |y[n]| first falls below 0.01.
difference-equations-and-stability.strategy_choice: Classify stability for (a) a recurrence given as y[n]=0.98y[n-1]+x[n] and (b) a measured impulse-response table with no stated recurrence by choosing between a characteristic-mode/root test and an absolute-summability test. The cue is whether exact recurrence coefficients or only response samples are available. Produce a classification with the applicable hypothesis and, for the finite table, state why the evidence cannot prove asymptotic stability.

perching-glider-system-identification.warm_up: Two held-out candidate models have residuals A=[0.10,-0.10,0.20,-0.20] and B=[0.02,-0.01,0.03,0.40] in lift-coefficient units. Compute each held-out RMSE, identify the model with lower aggregate error, and mark the structured terminal miss that the aggregate hides. Deliver a four-row residual table plus the two RMSE values.
perching-glider-system-identification.strategy_choice: For a time-ordered flight record whose final 20% contains the stall maneuver, choose between a random 80/20 split and a contiguous final-segment holdout. The deciding cue is temporal dependence and a deployment regime later than the fitted data, not sample count. Produce the chosen split diagram, train/test RMSE table, and a residual-versus-angle plot specification; explain in one sentence what leakage the rejected split permits.

complex-sinusoids-and-phasors.warm_up: Evaluate e^{j pi n/2} for n=0,1,2,3, tabulate its real and imaginary parts, and recover magnitude and wrapped phase at each index. Check that the real projection is zero at odd n while the complex magnitude remains one, and state why phase would be undefined if the magnitude were zero.
complex-sinusoids-and-phasors.strategy_choice: Estimate the amplitude of cos(0.3pi n+phi) over n=0,...,19 in two cases: (a) phi is calibrated to zero and (b) phi is unknown and may take any value. Choose between one real correlation and an I/Q correlation pair. The cue is whether input phase is known; produce both normalized estimator formulas and a phase sweep showing the single-projection null while the I/Q magnitude stays within 1% of the true amplitude.

dtft-and-frequency-response.warm_up: For h[n]=(1/3)[1,1,1] on n=0,1,2, derive H(e^{j omega}), then evaluate it at omega=0, pi/2, and 2pi/3. Report magnitude and phase where defined, and verify the exact 2pi/3 null by convolving six samples of e^{j2pi n/3} with h after startup.
dtft-and-frequency-response.strategy_choice: For (a) the steady-state output to one sinusoid through a known LTI filter and (b) the first six output samples to a finite pulse with zero initial state, choose between frequency-response multiplication and time-domain convolution. The cue is steady-state modal behavior versus transient/boundary information. Produce the selected computation for h=(1/3)[1,1,1] in each case and state the information discarded by the rejected method.

sampling-aliasing-and-reconstruction.warm_up: Sample cos(2pi·700t) and cos(2pi·300t) at f_s=1 kHz for n=0,...,5. Tabulate both sequences, reduce 700 Hz modulo the sampling lattice to its baseband alias, and show numerically that the records coincide. Mark where an analog anti-alias filter must act to prevent the ambiguity.
sampling-aliasing-and-reconstruction.strategy_choice: Choose between ordinary lowpass sampling and bandpass sampling for (a) a 0–4 kHz audio signal and (b) a narrow 20–21 kHz sensor band, given candidate rates 10 kHz and 6.4 kHz. The cue is the occupied spectral support and whether shifted replicas can remain disjoint, not the highest frequency alone. Produce a replica sketch for each selection and an anti-alias passband/stopband specification; reject any choice whose replicas overlap.

dft-bins-symmetry-and-scaling.warm_up: Compute the unnormalized eight-point DFT of x[n]=(-1)^n, identify the nonzero bin and its hertz value for f_s=8 kHz, then invert using the course's 1/N inverse scale. Check exact sample recovery and show how the reported coefficient magnitude changes under a unitary normalization.
dft-bins-symmetry-and-scaling.strategy_choice: For the same real eight-sample record, choose between a full two-sided complex DFT and a one-sided amplitude spectrum for (a) circular convolution by coefficient multiplication and (b) reporting physical sinusoid amplitudes to a reader. The cue is whether phase/negative-frequency coefficients are operationally required or conjugate symmetry may be collapsed. Produce a representation-and-scaling ledger and verify that neither representation double-counts DC or the Nyquist bin.

fft-factorization-and-layout.warm_up: Factor an eight-point DFT into three radix-2 stages. List the bit-reversed input order 0,4,2,6,1,5,3,7, count 12 butterfly twiddle multiplications versus 64 direct DFT products, and verify the factored output against direct evaluation for x=[1,2,3,4,0,0,0,0] to relative error below 1e-12.
fft-factorization-and-layout.strategy_choice: For (a) all 1024 coefficients of a streaming block and (b) only eight fixed DTMF frequencies from a 205-sample frame, choose between a full FFT and direct evaluation of the selected DFT sums. The cue is the number of requested frequencies relative to transform length together with latency and permutation cost. Produce a complex-operation and buffering ledger for both cases and require numerical agreement at the requested frequencies below 1e-10.

phone-channel-dtmf-receiver.warm_up: A 40 ms frame at 8 kHz has normalized detector energies {697:0.03, 770:0.82, 852:0.04, 941:0.02} and {1209:0.06, 1336:0.71, 1477:0.05, 1633:0.03}. With a 0.20 threshold and exactly-one-row/exactly-one-column rule, decode the key, compute the row/column twist in dB, and then explain why replacing 1336 Hz by a second above-threshold row tone must produce rejection rather than a key.
phone-channel-dtmf-receiver.strategy_choice: Design a receiver for two deployments by choosing between an FFT bank and eight Goertzel/matched complex detectors: (a) a 40 ms block processor that also needs a full diagnostic spectrum and (b) a low-memory controller that needs only the eight standard frequencies. The cues are requested-bin count, available block latency, and reuse of the full spectrum. Produce a decision table with multiplies, state memory, latency, and identical pass/reject results on one valid key and one single-tone impostor.

windows-leakage-and-resolution.warm_up: For the periodic four-sample Hann window w=[0,0.5,1,0.5], compute coherent gain (sum w)/N and ENBW N·sum(w^2)/(sum w)^2 in bins. Apply the window to a bin-centered sinusoid of amplitude one and show which correction recovers amplitude one; report the uncorrected bias and the 1.5-bin ENBW check.
windows-leakage-and-resolution.strategy_choice: Choose between a rectangular window and a four-term Blackman-Harris window for (a) separating two equal tones one main-lobe width apart and (b) detecting a tone 40 dB below a strong tone 5.5 bins away. The cue is whether main-lobe width or sidelobe rejection limits the claim. Produce a two-case selection table and specify the measured main-lobe-width and local-leakage checks that could overturn each choice.

peak-estimation-and-zero-padding.warm_up: A zero-padded spectrum has adjacent dB samples alpha=-12, beta=0, gamma=-6 at bins 19,20,21 with 10 Hz bin spacing. Use p=(1/2)(alpha-gamma)/(alpha-2beta+gamma) to estimate the fractional-bin offset and frequency, then state the zero-denominator boundary and the single-isolated-peak assumption needed for the estimate.
peak-estimation-and-zero-padding.strategy_choice: For (a) locating one isolated off-bin tone more precisely from a fixed 64-sample record and (b) separating two tones hidden inside that record's main lobe, choose between zero-padding plus peak interpolation and acquiring a longer record. The cue is localization of one modeled peak versus physical resolution of multiple components. Produce the selected acquisition/FFT plan and check main-lobe width in original-bin units so padding is not credited with added resolution.

correlation-psd-and-welch.warm_up: For x=[1,-1,1,-1], compute the biased autocorrelation estimates at lags 0,1,2,3 using denominator N and mirror the positive lags. Evaluate the resulting finite Fourier sum at omega=0 and pi. Report the lag convention and verify r_hat=[1,-0.75,0.5,-0.25], S_hat(0)=0, and S_hat(pi)=4 before interpreting the alternating sequence's high-frequency power.
correlation-psd-and-welch.strategy_choice: Estimate the PSD of a stationary 16,384-sample record containing two tones 0.04 cycles/sample apart in seeded white noise by choosing between one full-record periodogram and Welch averaging with shorter overlapped segments. The cue is the required tone separation versus estimator variance. Produce a predeclared segment/window/overlap choice, predicted resolution, and coefficient-of-variation check over 50 trials; reject a stable-looking estimate that merges the tones.

stft-spectrograms-and-reconstruction.warm_up: Use the periodic Hann samples [0,0.5,1,0.5] with hop R=2. Add three shifted windows over the interior timeline, tabulate the overlap sum, and verify it is constant at one away from boundaries. State the synthesis normalization and predict the amplitude modulation that appears if the hop is changed to three.
stft-spectrograms-and-reconstruction.strategy_choice: Analyze a signal containing a 12 ms click and two steady tones 40 Hz apart by choosing between 20 ms and 80 ms Hann STFT windows at 16 kHz. The cue is whether event timing or narrow frequency separation is the primary claim. Produce both parameter ledgers (sample count, hop, FFT length, bin spacing, latency), select one for each claim, and verify reconstruction with a normalized overlap-add null below -80 dB.

parametric-spectral-estimation.warm_up: For the AR(1) model x[n]=0.8x[n-1]+e[n] with unit innovation variance, compute S_xx(e^{j omega})=1/|1-0.8e^{-j omega}|^2 at omega=0 and pi. Report the peak-to-trough ratio and confirm that the pole radius is below one before calling the model stationary.
parametric-spectral-estimation.strategy_choice: For (a) broadband noise with no defensible low-order model and (b) a short record generated by a stable AR(2) resonance, choose between Welch estimation and an AR/Yule-Walker spectrum. The cue is whether a low-order generative model survives residual-whiteness and held-out checks, not whether its plotted peak is sharper. Produce the selected spectrum, order/segment rationale, held-out residual test, and a comparison showing any unsupported peaks.

recorded-audio-spectral-analysis.warm_up: At f_s=16 kHz, convert a 25 ms window and 10 ms hop to samples, choose N_FFT=512, compute the FFT grid spacing, and determine the number of complete frames in a 1.000 s clip without end padding. Deliver a parameter ledger and check that changing N_FFT alone changes grid density but not the 25 ms observation duration.
recorded-audio-spectral-analysis.strategy_choice: For (a) estimating the average noise floor of a steady 500 ms oboe sustain and (b) locating moving speech formants across a one-second utterance, choose between Welch PSD averaging and an order-preserving STFT. The cue is whether frame order is disposable under a stationary claim or is itself evidence. Produce the chosen parameter ledger, a neighboring-frame stability check for every claimed harmonic/formant, and a phase-preserving reconstruction null below -80 dB for the STFT path.
